entries.title: Leviticus 1:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A Continuation of the former Hiſtorie, from the rearing of the Tabernacle, to the numbering of the people; beeing the hiſtorie of one moneth onely.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Bring an offering] Whereby they were led to Chriſt; as the Apoſtle ſheweth in that excellent Epiſtle to the Hebrews; which is a juſt Commentarie upon this Book.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Burnt ſacrifice] A whole-burnt-off[ilegible]ring. Heb 10.6. purporting whole Chri[ilegible], uffering for us Iſa. 53 12 and our ſacrificing our whole ſelvs to him, [ilegible]s a reaſonable ſervice. Rom. 12.1

entries.title: Leviticus 1:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And hee ſhall put his hand] As acknowledging his own guilt, and transferring the ſame upon Chriſt, reſting upon him with full aſſurance of faith, handfaſting us unto him.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And bee ſhall kill the bullock] The Prieſt ſhall kill it: for it was death for anie man to offer his own ſacrifice; ſo it is ſtill for anie to com to God, otherwiſe then in, and by Chriſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And hee ſhall flaie the burnt-offering] To ſhew the grievouſneſs of our Saviour's ſufferings; the cruel uſage of his ſuffering Saints. Micah 3.3. Heb. 11.35. and the dutie of all that have benefit by him, to flea off the old man with his deceitful luſts. Epheſ. 4.22. dealing thereby as the Turk dealt by him that betraied the Rhodes. (L[ilegible]unclav.) Hee preſented unto him his promiſed wife and portion: but withal told him, that hee would not have a Chriſtian to bee his ſon-in-law: and therefore cauſſed his Baptized skin (as hee called it) to bee flaied off, and him to bee caſt into a bed ſtrawed with ſalt, that hee might get a new skin. See Mark 9.49.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Fire upon the Altar] That ſire from heaven. Lev. 9.24. (which the Heathens apiſhly imitated in their Veſtal fire.) Typing either the ſcorching wrath of God ſeiſing upon Chriſt, or the ardent love of Chriſt to his, and their zeal for him.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In order upon the wood] Shewing, that Miniſters muſt rightly divide, and diſpoſe the Word of God. 2 Tim. 2.15. and evidently ſet forth Chriſt crucified. Gal. 3.1.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall hee waſh] Shadowing Chriſt's perfect puritie. Heb. 7. and our intire ſanctification. Ezek. 26.35. Heb. 10.22. [Of a ſweet ſavor unto the Lord] The burning and broiling of the beaſts could yield no ſweet ſavor; but thereto was added wine, oil, and incenſ, by God's appointment, and then there was a ſavor of reſt in it. Our praiers, as from us, would never pleaſ; but as indited by the Spirit, and preſented by Chriſt, they are highly accepted in heaven.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A male without blemiſh] But curſed bee that coſener that hath in his flock a male, and ſacrificeth unto God a corrupt thing. Mal. 1.14.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: On the ſide of the Altar, northward] Not Eaſtward as the Heathen ſacrifices: or to note the obſcuritie of the Legal Cetimonies.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In order] See the Note on Verſ 8.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall waſh] See the Note on Verſ 9.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Turtle doves, or young pigeons] Old turtles and young pigeons are the beſt: God muſt have the verie beſt of the beſt, as beeing beſt-worthie.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Wring off his head] Or, pinch it with his nail, that the blood might go out, without ſeparating it from the reſt of the bodie. This figured the death of Chriſt, without either breaking a bone, or dividing the God-head from the manhood. As alſo the skill that ſhould bee in Miniſters, to cut or divide aright the word of truth.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: His crop with his feathers] Or the maw with the filth thereof (that is, the guts which receiv the filth ſent unto them from the maw) was pluckt out, and the blood ſtrained at the ſide of the Altar: this ſignified thoſe clods of blood wrung from our Saviour, before his oblation upon the Croſs.

entries.title: Leviticus 1:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A[ilegible]d hee ſhall cleav it] That the inward part might bee laid on the fire. See Pſal. 51.18, 19. Mark 12.33.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: NO quantitie is here preſcribed, becauſ it was a Free-will-offering: onely it muſt bee fine, no bran in it: to ſhew the puritie of Chriſt's ſacrifice. Heb. 7.26. and of our ſervices through him. Mal. 3.11. By means of the oil of his Spirit, and incenſ of his Interceſſion.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall burn the memorial of it] Whereby God was inminded (as it were) of the partie offering, and acknowledging all his ſtore to bee from God.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall bee Aaron's and his ſons] As meat for them: hence it was called a Meat-offering; and ſent them to Chriſt, the meat that endureth unto life everlaſting. John 6.27.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋnleavened cake, mingled with oil] Sinceritie is the mother of ſerenitie; Truth, of tranquillitie.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Baken in a pan] Afterwards parted in pieces, and oil powred upon it: ſignified the graces of God's Spirit wherewith Chriſt was fully annointed within and without. Pſalm 45.8. and wherewith wee ſhould bee tempered and annointed. 1 John 2.27. 2 Cor. 1.21.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And pour oil thereon] Jacob was the firſt wee read of that conſecrated his offerings with oil. Gen. 28.18. Probably hee had it from his predeceſſors.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Baken in the frying-pan] So, My heart is frying of a good matter, ſaith David. Pſalm 45.1.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall bring it unto the Altar] God would have all their offerings brought to one Altar; both to figure out the one onely all-ſufficient-ſacrifice of Chriſt, and to teach all the faithful to conſent in one and the ſame truth of the Goſpel.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Amemorial thereof] Signifying the perpetual benefit of Chriſt's death to all believers.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall be Aaron's and his ſon's] Miniſters maintenence.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Nor anie honie] Which hath a leavening virtue in it. Sweet ſins are to bee abandoned: there will bee bitterneſs in the end. Prov. 26.26, 27.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Yee ſhall offer them] i. e. With the firſt-fruits yee ſhall offer both leven. Lev. 23.17. and honie. 2 Chron. 31.5. Both which are ſomtimes taken in the better part. Mat. 13.33. Cant. 4.11.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shalt thou ſeaſon with ſalt] Called here the ſalt of Gods's covenant; as ſignifying the covenant of God, made with us in Chriſt, who ſeaſoneth us, and make's all our ſervices ſavorie. See the Note on Mark 9.49, 50.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Green ears of corn] To ſignifie that God ſhould bee ſerved with the firſt-fruits of our age, the primroſe of our childe-hood.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: IN Chriſt, there is neither male nor female, but all one. Gal. 3, 28. Souls have no ſexes. In Thank-offerings, the female alſo might paſs: to teach, that God look's not ſo much to the worth of the gift, as the honeſtie of the heart that offer's it. Leavened bread alſo in this caſe was accepted. Lev. 7.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the Altar round about] This ſignified that plenteous redemption by the blood of ſprinkling.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The fat that covereth the inwards] Heartie thanks muſt bee given to God; ſuch as cometh not from the roof of the mouth, but the root of the heart. An aërie, God bee thanked, profiteth not. Sing with grace in your hearts, is the beſt tune to anie Pſalm. The voice which is made in the mouth is nothing ſo ſweet as that which com's from the depth of the breaſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With the kidnies] Thoſe ſeats of Luſts. Earth lie members muſt bee mortified by the thankful.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the burnt-ſacrifice] Which was firſt offered; to teach us, that ſin muſt bee pardoned ere our Thank-offerings can bee accepted. It is therefore (ordinarily) beſt to begin our praiers with confeſſion of ſin, and petitions for pardon through Chriſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Laie his hand] See the Note on Chap. 1. v. 4.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The whole [ilegible]ump.] Which in thoſe countrie-ſheep is verie large yet not ſo large as thoſe in America, (The world encompaſſed.) mentioned by Sr. Francis Drake, as big as kine, and ſupplying the room of horſes for burthen, or travel.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It is the food] That whereupon God himſelf ſeemeth to feed. Pſalm 50.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 3:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That yee neither eat fat, nor blood] Neither bee carnal nor cruel, but let your ſouls delight in the fatneſs and ſweetneſs of God's ordinances.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: OR infirmitie; beeing ſuddenly ſurpriſed, preoccupated Gal. 6.1. See the Note there, and on Heb 5.2.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A young bullock] The ſame ſacrifice that ſhould bee offered for the ſin of the whole people. Verſ 14. To note the hainouſneſs of the Prieſt's ſin above others. The ſins of Teachers, are the Teachers of ſins.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall laie his hand] Confeſſing his ſin. Lev. 5.5. and profeſſing his faith in Chriſt the true ſin-offering. 2 Cor. 5.21.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall take of the bullocks blood] See Heb. 5.2, 3. and 7.26, 27, 28. with the Notes there.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Seven times before the Lord] Becauſ in this caſe, there was need of much and great purgation.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the borns of the Altar] To ſignifie (ſaith one) that the preaching of the Goſpel concerning the blood of Chriſt, ſhould bee publiſhed and proclaimed to the four corners of the earth. To ſhew (ſaith another) that by faith in the bloud of Chriſt, our praiers are acceptable unto God, and our infirmities pardoned and purged.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: All the fat] Becauſ (among other things) it ſignified hard-heartedneſs and inſenſibleneſs of ſin and danger. Pſal. 119.70. Dionyſius the Heracleot felt not needles thruſt into his fat bellie, ſaith the hiſtorie.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With the kidnies] See Chap 3.4.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the skin, &c.] See the Note on Chap. 1.9.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall hee carrie forth] Heb. 13.11, 12. See the Notes.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And of the whole congregation] Particular congregations then may err for a ſeaſon; though not finally, fundamentally, if they bee the congregation of Saints. Pſal. 89.5. and not of Hypocrites. Job 15.34. the Church malignant. [And they have don ſomwhat] Either by tranſgreſſion or diſobedience. Hel. 2.2. on [ilegible]ion or commiſſion.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: When the ſin is known] Sin may ſleep a long time like a ſleeping d[ilegible]bt, not called for of manie years: but Nullum tempus occurrit Regi, God may ſend out a ſummons for ſleepers, and puniſh our by-gon or ſecret ſins.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the Elders] Theſe as the repreſentative congregation, took upon them the guilt of their common errors, as thoſe did. 2 Chron. 29 23.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the Prieſt that is annointed] i. e. The High-prieſt a type of Chriſt, who was annointed, not with material oil, as they, but with the Spirit, that oil of gladneſs both above, and for his fellow-brethren. Pſal. 45. Heb. 1. See 1 John 2.27. and 2 Cor. 1.21, 22. Howbeit his oil ſhine's brighteſt, and ſwim's a-loft above all others.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Seven times A number of perfection; to note the moſt abſolute ſufficiencie of Chriſt's death to purge and reconcile us to God; ([ilegible].) and that hee is able to ſave ſuch to the uttermoſt that com unto God by him. Heb. 7.25.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the borns] See the Note on Verſ 7. [At the bottom of the Altar] To ſet forth the plentie and ſufficiencie of Grace and Merit in Chriſt's death, for manie more then are actually ſaved by it.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And hee ſhall take all his fat] Chriſt offered himſelf and the beſt parts [ilegible] had; ſuffering in ſoul and bodie.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: As hee did with the bullock] For even ignorance and infirmities are deadlie ſins, direct fruits of the fleſh. John 3.6. and ſuch as for which Chriſt laid down his life, ([ilegible].) even for the notknowings of the people. Heb. 9.7.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Without the camp] Pointing to Chriſt, who carried our ſins out of God's light. See Heb. 13.12. with the Note.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: When a ruler hath ſinned] Great men's ſins do more hurt, 1. By imitation, for Vita principis cenſura eſt, imò Cynoſura, according to theſe glaſſes moſt men dreſs themſelvs. 2. imputation; for plectuntur Achivi, the poor people paie for it; as they did for David's, whether ignorance or infirmitie, in omitting that dutie enjoined Exod. 30.12, 13, 14, 15. thence the plague. 2 Sam. 24.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Com to his knowledg] As David's did. 2 Sam. 24. who ſaw ſuch volumes of infirmities, and ſo manie Errata's in all that hee did, that hee once cried out, Who knoweth the errors of his life? Oh cleanſ mee from ſecret ſins. Pſal. 19.12. This hee knew was the import of all theſe Levitical cleanſings.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Laie his hand] See the Note on Verſ 4.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: At the bottom] See Verſ 18.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:26
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: All his fat] See Verſ 19. The fat was burnt (ſaith one) becauſ (among other things) it ſignified duricordium, hardheartedneſs. Pſal. 119.70.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:27
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And if a ſoul ſin] As there is none that liveth and ſinneth not. 2 King. 8.46. Triſte mortalitatis privilegium eſt licere aliquando peccare. (Ephor. Auguſta nimis res eſt, & nulli mortalium conceſſa nuſpiam errare. Amana.)

entries.title: Leviticus 4:28
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Com to his knowledg] By the check of his own conſcience, awakened by the word or rod of God.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And ſlaie the Sin-offering] That is, the Prieſt ſhall: for no man might offer his own ſacrifice upon pain of death; as is afore noted.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:31
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For a ſweet ſavor] See the Note on Chap. 1. verſ 9. The death of Chriſt is ever in the fight of his heaven he father: and hence it was, that thoſe typical ſacrifices, and all our performances are [ilegible]ill accepted.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: HEe ſhall ſuffer for his ſinfull ſilence; becauſ hee could, but would not help the truth in neceſſiti[ilegible], but ſtand as it hee were gag'd by Satan, poſſeſt with a dumb divel.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And if it bee hidden from him] Debt is debt whether a man know of it, or not.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Then hee ſhall bee guiltie] Guiltie hee was before ver. 2. but now hee ſhall ſee him [ilegible]o, and bee readie to ſaie as Prov 5 14. I was almoſt in all evil, in the midst of the congregation and the aſſemblie By the law is the knowledg of ſin. Rom 3.20.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
And it bee hid f[ilegible]om him] As is uſual with your common ſwearers, who will ſwear that they ſwear not. If men had ſuch diſtemper of bodie, as their excrements came from them when they knew not of it, it would trouble them; but they ſwear, and let go much filth, and it is hid from them.

To do evil] As David did to ſlaie Nabal 1 Sam. 25.22.

Or to do good] As the ſame David did to do good to Mephiboſheth and yet hee was not [ilegible]o good as his oath.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Hee ſhall confeſs] Homo agnoſcit, Deus ignoſcit. Man confeſſeth, and God pardoneth. In the courts of men it is the ſafeſt plea to ſaie, Non feci (quoth Quintilian) I am not guiltie: not ſo here; but ego feci, miſerere, I did it, have mercie upon mee.

Per miſerere mei tollitur ira Dei.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For his ſin which hee hath ſinned] Bending his thoughts upon that particular ſin, it is charged upon I[ilegible]raël, Ezek. 16.22. that they remembred not that they laie in their blood

entries.title: Leviticus 5:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Two turtle Doves] See the Note on Chap. 114.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For the ſin-offering firſt] For till un bee expi[ilegible]ted, no ſacrifice or ſervice can bee accepted. Therefore Iſa. 1. Waſh you, [ilegible]anſ you, and then com and let us reaſon.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the ſide of the Altar] The North-ſide, and not upon the Eaſt: 1. that Iſraël might not ſymbolize with the Heathens, who worſhipped toward the Eaſt: 2. to ſignifie that they had no more under the Law then dark ſhadows of good things to com. Heb. 10.1. until the time of reformation. Heb. 9.10.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: According to the manner.] That is, the forms and rites preſcribed. So Amos 8.14. The manner of Beerſheba, i.e. the forms and rites of worſhipping in Beerſheba, as the Caldee paraphraſeth it.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But if hee bee not able] So low doth the moſt High ſtoop to man's meanneſs, that hee will accept of a verie ſmall preſent from him that would bring a better, if it were in the power of his hand. Lycurgus enjoyned his Lacedemonians to offer ſmall ſacrifices, For God (ſaid hee) reſpecteth more the internal devotion, then the external oblation.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Even a memorial] This is ſpoken after the manner of men who have need of remembrancers. God ſomtimes ſeem's to loſe his mercie, and then wee muſt finde it for him, as they Iſa. 63.15. ſomtimes to forget, ſleep, delaie, &c. and then wee muſt in-minde, awaken, quicken him. Iſa. 62.7.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And it ſhall bee forgiven him] See a like promiſs made to our Miniſterie. Jam. 5.15.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In the bolie things of the Lord] Things conſecrate to him, by robbing and wronging of God and his Prieſts; bee it but through ignorance or error. (Sacrum qui clepſerit, rapſeritve, parricida eſte.) For to do ſuch a thing preſumptuouſly was death. Numb. 15.30. and by the laws of the twelv Tables in Rome, ſuch were to bee puniſhed as parricides.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And hee ſhall make amends] No remiſſion without reſtitution. God abhors holocauſtum ex rapina. (Latimer's Sex.) And if yee make no reſtitution, ye ſhall cough in hell, ſaid father Latimer.

entries.title: Leviticus 5:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Though hee wiſt not] Ignorance, though invincible and unavoidable, well may excuſe à tanto, but not à toto. Luke 12.48.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
AS David in defiling his neighbours wiſe, and afterwards killing him, is ſaid to have deſpiſed the commandment of the Lord, and to have don evil in his ſight. 2 Sam. 12.9. which alſo hee penitently acknowledgeth. Pſal. 51.4. Sin is properly againſt none but God, (Godw. Heb. Antiq. p. 98.) beeing a tranſgreſſion of his law. Hence the manſlaier was confined to the Citie of refuge as to a priſon, during the life of the high-Prieſt; as beeing (ſaith one) the chief God on earth. That was a true poſition of the Pelagians, Omne peccatum eſt contemptus Dei, that everie ſin is a contempt of God. Prov. 18.3.

In fellowſhip] Heb. (Job 8.20. Dextram conjungere dextrâ. Quid non mortalia pectora cogit. Auri ſacra fames? [ilegible].) Heb. In putting of the hand. It is ſaid in Iob, that God will not take a wicked man by the hand, i. e. hee will have no fellowſhip with him.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And lieth concerning it, and ſweareth falſty] Thorough inordinate love of money, that root of all evil; but ſuch monie ſhall periſh with them. Zech. 5.2.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And is guiltie] Found guiltie by a ſelf-condemning conſcience; which now like Samſon's wife conceal's not the riddle, but tel's all, as ſhee ſaid of our Saviour. Iohn 4.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In the daie of his treſpaſs offering] Before hee compaſs God's altar. Mat. 5.23. with the Note there.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With thy eſtimation] i. e. as thou ſhalt rate it. Moſes did the Prieſts office for preſent. Hee was likewiſe a Prophet. Deut. 18.15. and King in Ieſhurun. Deut. 33.5. and ſo became a type of Chriſt that true Triſmegiſt, the Prieſt, Prophet and Prince. Dan. 9.25.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall make an attonement] Thorough the ſacrifice of Chriſt. Heb. 10.1, 4, 10, 14.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: All night until the morning] God muſt bee thought upon in the night ſeaſon. Pſal. 4.4. David willingly brake his ſleep to do it. Pſal. 119.62. The daie is thine, the night alſo is thine, ſaith hee. Pſal. 74.16.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Beſides the altar] On the Eaſt-ſide, furtheſt from the Sanctuarie. Levit. 1.16. in reverence of the divine majeſtie.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In a clean place] Becauſ they came from the Lord's holie houſ. See the contrarie commanded concerning the ſtones and duſt of a leprous houſ. Levit. 14.40.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It ſhall not bee put out] No more ſhould our faith, love, zeal, (that flame of God as Solomon cal's it. Cant. 8.6.) that ſhould never go out; the waters ſhould not quench it, nor the aſhes cover it. Cant. 8.10. 2 Tim. 1.6.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The fire ſhall ever bee burning] The Gentiles (by an apiſh imitation hereof) had their veſtal fire, ſalted meal, and manie other ſacred rites. Baſil chargeth the divel as a thief of the truth, in that hee had decked his crows with her fethers.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The law of the meat-offering] Beſides what is ſet down: chap. 2.1, 2. Thus one text explain's another; as the diamond is brightened with its own duſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Even the memorial] See the Note on Levit. 2.2.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall Aaron and his ſons eat] See 1 Cor. 9.13, 14. with the Note there.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It ſhall not bee baken with leaven] Which is, 1. ſouring; 2. ſwelling; 3. ſpreading; 4. impuring.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall bee holie] God will bee ſanctified in all that draw near unto him—procul binc procul eſte profani.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: When hee is anointed] i. e. When anie high-prieſt: for hee onely was anointed. Exod. 29.7. on the head at leaſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In a pan] Figuring out the ſufferings of Chriſt, who was ſo parched with the fire of afflictions for our ſins.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It ſhall not bee eaten] To teach the high-prieſt to look [ilegible]or ſalvation out of himſelf.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In the place] i. e. at the North-ſide of the altar. And why, ſee the Note on Chap. 5.9.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:26
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall eat it] Except in that caſe. verſ 30.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:27
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall bee holie] This taught an holie uſe of the myſterie of our redemption: for the ſin-offering in ſpecial ſort figured Chriſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:28
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But the earthen veſsel] So contagious a thing is ſin, that it defileth the verie viſible heaven and earth: which therefore muſt bee likewiſe purged by the laſt fire, as the earthen pot which held the ſin-offering was broken, and the braſen ſcoured and rinſed in water.

entries.title: Leviticus 6:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And no ſin-offering] Here the ordinarie gloſs make's this obſervation, Remiſsionem dare, Dei ſolius eſt, qui per ignem ſignificatur: That to pardon ſin belong's to God alone, who is a conſuming fire. The Rhemiſts tell us of a man that could remove mountains: (Rhem. Annot. in Jo[ilegible]. 20. Sect. 3.) which they may aſſoon perſwade us, as that their Prieſts have as full power to pardon ſins, as Chriſt had. One of their Prieſts meeting with a man troubled in minde, told him that their religion afforded more comfort to the conſcience then ours; and that becauſ it had, and exerciſed a power to pardon ſin; (M. Ley his patte[ilegible]n of pietie. p. 145.) which our Miniſters neither did, nor durſt aſſume to themſelvs.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A Sham, Piaculum, quo peccatum expiabatur. How it differed from the ſin-offering is hard to determine.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In the place] See the Note on Chap. 1.11.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That covereth the inwards▪] My ſon give mee thy heart. See Pſal. 51.6. Jer. 4 14.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the two kidneys] See the Note on Lev. 3.4.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: As the ſin-offering is] They were diſtinct then. See verſ 1.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Priest ſhall have to himſelf] It is a ſign of gaſping devotion, when men are ſo ſtreight-handed to their Miniſters, who ſhould have part of all. Gal. 6.6.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And all the meat-offering] Which ſeem's to bee ſo called, partly becauſ it went as meat unto the Prieſt (the laborer is ſurely worthie of his meat. Mat. 10.10.) but principally as leading to Chriſt, whoſe fleſh is meat indeed. John 6.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Have one as much as another] In their father's houſ was bread enough. Put mee, I praie thee into one of the Prieſts offices, that I may cat a piece of bread. 1 Sam. 2.36. This the Tirſhata would not ſuffer thoſe turn-coats to do. Ezra 2.63. But how hard put too[ilegible]t was that poor Prieſt, that anſwer'd young Pareüs, (Vita Parei per Philipp: filtum, primo oper: tom[ilegible] praefixa.) asking him an alms (according to the cuſtom of thoſe times) Nos pauperi fratres, nos nihil habemus, an piſcimus, an caro, an panis, an miſericordia babemus?

entries.title: Leviticus 7:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Sacrifice of peace-offering] Or, Paie-offering. See Pſal. 116.14. I will paie, or, I will perfect. Fitly: for a vow, till paid is an imperfect thing.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋnlevened cakes] There muſt bee ſinceritie in all our ſervices: for elſ God will not once look at them.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Levened bread] Lo, levened bread will paſs in a peace-offering: God for Chriſts ſake reject's not the ſervices of his Saints, though tainted with corruption. (August.) Peccata nobis non nocent, ſi non placent. Wine is not thrown awaie for the dregs, nor gold for the dirt, that cleav's unto it.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For an heav-offering] So called, becauſ it was heaved and lifted up before the Lord, in token that they received all from him, and did acknowledg all to be due to him.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Eaten the ſame daie] Thanks muſt bee returned whiles mercies are freſh; leſt, as fiſh, they putrefie with keeping. Eaten bread is ſoon forgotten. Hezekiah wrote his ſong the third daie after his recoverie. Jehoſuphat gave thanks, firſt upon the ground where hee had the victorie, calling it Berachah; and three daies after again at Jeruſalem, 2 Chron. 20. See David's Now, Now, Now, I will paie my vows. Pſalm 116.14, 15.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: On the third daie] Foreſhadowing the reſurrection of Chriſt on the third daie, whereby all legal Cerimonies were aboliſh[ilegible]d, and had no uſe in the Church, but by accident; as hee who buildeth a vault, letteth the centrels ſtand till hee put in the kei[ilegible]-ſtone, and then pulleth them awaie.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It ſhall bee an abomination] Kept beyond the time; and ſo uneatable, unſacrificeable, prophane, ſtinking.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall not bee eaten] Becauſ not fit to repreſent Chriſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Having his uncleanneſs upon him] To the unclean all things are unclean. &c. Tit. 1.15. See the Note.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Cut off from his people] Confer 1 Cor. 11.27, 28, 29.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the Lord ſpa[ilegible]e unto Moſes] This is oſt repeted to draw attention and get autoritie. See 1 Theſ. 2.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: No manner fat] See the Note on Levit 3.12.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋſed in anie other uſe] Though not in Sacrifice. Mudwals may bee made up of any refuſe matter: not ſo, the wals of a Church or Palace.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall bee cut off] i. e. Shall bee liable to God's judgments.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:26
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Yee ſhall eat no manner of blood]. This ſignified. 1. That wee ſhould learn to honor holie things, and not to make a mock of them by employing them to common uſe. 2. That wee ſhould bee moſt careful not to ſhed man's blood, for the ſatisfying of our luſt. See Levit. 17.11, 12. with Gen. 9.4, 5. and Deut. 12.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋnto the Lord] Not kill it in the Camp, though there they might eat it.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
His own hands] Teaching them that they muſt live by their own faith. Hab. 2.5.

May bee waved] Or, Shaken to and fro; which ſignified the ſhaking of our lips, in giving thanks to God. Hoſ. 14.2. Heb. 13.15, 16. which yet muſt bee fetcht lower then the lips, even from the bottom of the heart; the deeper the ſweeter. The voice that is made in the mouth is nothing ſo ſweet, as that which com's from the depth of the breſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:31-32
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The breſt ſhall bee Aarons, and the right ſhoulder] To note, that men muſt give their breſts and ſhoulders, affections and actions, even their whole ſelvs; firſt to the Lord, and then to us Miniſters by the will of God, as thoſe famous Macedonians did. 2 Cor. 8.5. that ſo they may bee ſani in doctrina & ſancti in vita, ſound in doctrine, and holie in life.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:34
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For the wave breſt, and the right ſhoulder] This might further ſignifie (ſaith one) that Chriſt Jeſus heaved up for us both breſt and ſhoulder, that is, wiſdom and ſtrength to all his elect Prieſthood, whoſe portion hee is. 1 Cor. 1 30. Or it might note (ſaith another) that Miniſters ſhould both take care (figured by the breſt) and pains (ſignified by the ſhoulder.) And therefore the high-prieſt did to that end wear the names of the Tribes upon his ſhoulders, and upon his breſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 7:35
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: This is the portion of the anointing] That is, of the anointed Prieſts; and that becauſ they were anointed to the office. Here Origen (according to his manner) turn's all into allegories and myſteries, and tel's us of a three-fold ſenſ of Scripture, 1. Literal. 2. Moral. 3. Myſtical; comparing them to the gridiron, frying-pan, and oven, uſed in dreſſing the meat-offering, (Allegorias ſpumam ſcriprurae vocat. Luth. in Gen. 3. p. 67.) verſ 9. of this Chapter. But this itch of all allegorizing dark and difficult texts hath no ſmall danger in it. And I may doubt of Origen, as one doth of Hierom, Ʋtrùm plus boni peritiâ ling[ilegible]arum, quâ excelluit, an mali ſuis allegoriis, in quibus dominatus fuit, Eccleſiae Dei attulerit; (Amama Ant[ilegible]batb.) whether hee did more hurt or good to the Church.

entries.title: Leviticus 8:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: SEE the Note on Lev. 7.22. And for the reſt of the Chapter, read the Notes on Exod. 28. & 29. & 30.

entries.title: Leviticus 8:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And gather thou all the congregation] Miniſters are to bee ordeined in the publick Aſſemblie. Acts 14.22. that the people may ſhew their approbation, profeſs their purpoſe of obedience, and praie for God's Spirit to bee poured upon them.

entries.title: Leviticus 8:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And Moſes brought Aaron] They did not intrude themſelvs. See the Note on Heb. 5.4.

entries.title: Leviticus 8:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee put in the breſt-plate the Ʋrim, &c.] Hence (it may bee) God appointed the breſt-plate to bee made double, that the Urim and Thummim might bee put within, and lie hid on everie ſide. This Urim and Thummim ſignified (ſaith one) that in Chriſt are hidden all the treaſures of wiſdom and knowledg. Col. 2.3. and that hee hath all ſecret things moſt perfectly known and numbred out before him, which hee revealeth continually to his Church and choſen, as need requireth, by ſuch means as himſelf hath ſanctified. Pſal. 25.14, John 14.21, 26. & 17.14, 17, 26.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: THe verie next daie after the Prieſt's conſecration, that no time might bee loſt. I made haſte and delaied not, &c. Pſalm 119.16. Then ſaid I, lo I com: in the volume of the book it is written of mee, &c. Pſalm. 40.7. Live, live, live, (ſaith one) quickly, much, long: let no water go by, no daie bee loſt, &c. Preach, preach, bee inſtant, quick at work, &c.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Take thee alyoung calf] In remembrance, and ſor the remiſſion of Aaron's ſin about the golden calf; as ſom Hebrews are of opinion.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Take yee a kid of the goats for a Sin-offering] Quia gravis odor peccati, The ſmell of ſin is grievous; it offendeth all God's ſenſes, yea, his verie ſoul. Iſa. 1.12, 13. &c.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For to daie the Lord will appear unto you] And hee may not ſinde you emptie-handed, unprepared. See the Notes on Fxod. 19.10.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the glorie of the Lord ſhall appear unto you] ſo ſhall it one daie to us: yea, wee ſhall bee like him, and appear with him in glorie; and muſt therefore purifie our ſelvs, as God is pure. 1 John 3.2, 3.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Make attonement for thy ſelf] See Heb. 5.3. & 7.27, 28. with the Notes there.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Went unto the Altar] i. e. The braſen Altar; for hee had not yet acceſs to the Altar of Incenſ. Wee muſt ſtaie our corruptions, before wee preſent our ſupplications; waſh our hearts from wickedneſs, and then compaſs God's Altar.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Lift up his hands] Hee put the bleſſing upon them. A type of Chriſt. Luke 24.50. with Acts 3.26. Epheſ. 1.3.

entries.title: Leviticus 9:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: They ſhouted, and fell on their faces] The conſideration of God's gracious acceptation of us in Chriſt, ſhould make us to lift manie an humble, joiful, and thankful heart to God.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: THeſe jollie young Prieſts, over-joied haply of their new emploiment, and over-warmed with wine (as ſom gather out of Verſ 9.) over-ſhoot themſelvs the verie daie of their ſervice. Verſ 19. and are ſuddenly ſurpriſed by a doleful death. So was that inconſiderate Prieſt o[ilegible] Naples, Anno Dom. 1457. of whom Wolphius report's, (Wolph. Mcmorab. Lect. C[ilegible]. 15.) that when the hill Veſuvius had ſent huge flames, and don great ſpoil; hee, to make proof of his pietie, read a Maſs, and would need's go up the hill to finde out the cauſ of ſuch a calamitie. But for a reward of his foolhardineſs, hee periſhed in the flames, and was never heard of anie more.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And there went out fire] By fire they ſinned; and by fire they periſhed. Per quod quis peccat, per idem punitur & ipſe: Neſtorii lingua vermibus exeſa eſt. (Evag. lib, 1.) So Archbiſhop Arundel's tongue rotted in his head. The Archbiſhop of Tours in France made ſuit for the erection of a Court called Chambre Ardent, wherein to condemn the Proteſtants to the fire. Hee was afterwards ſtricken with a diſeaſ called the fire of God, (Act. and Mon. fol. 1911.) which began at his feet and ſo aſſcended upward, that hee cauſſed one member after another to be cut off, and ſo hee died miſerably.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: This is that the Lord ſpake] Where? and when? Lev. 8.35. Exod. 19.22. Or perhaps no where written, but at ſom other time ſpoken by God. Moſes might but ſet down the ſhort Notes of his diſcourſes, as the Prophets uſed to do. [I will bee ſanctified] Either actively or paſſively, Aut à nobis, aut in nos, either in us or upon us; ſure it is, that hee will bee no loſer by us. Sanctified hee will bee, either in the ſinceritie of men's converſation, or elſ in the ſeveritie of their condemnation. Singular things are exſpected of all that draw nigh to God in anie dutie, but eſpecially in the office of the Miniſterie. Thoſe that ſtand in the preſence of Princes muſt bee exact in their carriages. God appointed both the weights and meaſures of the Sanctuarie to bee twice as large as thoſe of the Commonwealth; to ſhew, that hee exſpect's much more of thoſe that ſerv him there, then hee doth of others. The ſouls of Prieſts muſt bee purer then the ſun-beams ſaith Chryſoſtom. (D. Hakw. on Pſalm 101.) [And Aaron held his peace] Hee bridled his paſſions, and ſubmitted to the divine Juſtice. The like did David. Pſalm 39.9. which words were taken up by Du-pleſſis in the loſs of his onely ſon.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In their coats] Theſe were not burnt, as neither were their bodies: the fire, (Toſtat.) beeing of a celeſtial and ſubtile nature, might pierce their inward parts, not touching their outward: as the lightning kill's by piercing, not by burning.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And Moſes ſaid unto Aaron] Philo reporteth, that the High-prieſt of the Jews, to keep alwaies his ſoul pure, never ſaw anie mournful object. Tiberius, counterfeiting grief at the funeral of Druſus, had a veil laid betwixt the dead and him, that hee might not ſee the bodie, becauſ hee was (as the reſt of the Emperors alſo were) Pontifex Maximus, or the High-prieſt; and therefore a ſacred perſon. Mourning in Aaron might have ſeemed murmuring: hee is therefore forbidden it, and accordingly hee forbear's. (Manlii Loc. com. p. 215.) So did Luther when hee buried his daughter, hee was not ſeen to ſhed a tear. No more did reverend Mr. William Whatelie late Paſtor of Banburie, when after hee had preached his own childe's Funeral upon this Text, The will of the Lord bee don: hee and his wiſe laid the childe in the grave with their own hands. [Bewail the burning] It's fit enough (ordinarily) that the bodie, when ſown in corruption, bee watered by the tears of thoſe that plant it in the earth.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For the annointing oil of the Lord is upon you] This is everie true Chriſtian's caſe, who ſhould therefore carrie himſelf accordingly. There is a [ilegible], a ſeemlie carriage belong's to everie calling. You have an unction, &c. 1 John 2.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Do not drink wine, nor ſtrong drink] As ſom are of opinion Nadab and Abihu had don; (Ex malis moribus honae leges.) which miſcarriage of theirs occaſioned this precept. The perpetual equitie whereof is, that Miniſters bee no wine-blbbers or Aleſtakes. 1 Tim. 3.3. Why ſhould it bee ſaid as of old, They have erred becauſ of wine, and have gon out of the waie becauſ of ſtrong drink, even the Prieſt and the Prophet? Iſa. 28.7. Drunkenneſs is a crime in all, but it's a kinde of Sacrilege in Miniſters. And if other drunkards deſerv double puniſhments for their miſdemeanours, (as Ariſtotle judgeth) firſt for their drunkenneſs, ([ilegible]. Ariſt. Ethic. lib. 3. c. 5) and then for the ſin committed in, and by their drunkenneſs; what do drunken Prieſts? Iſa. 56.12.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And that yee may put difference] Drunkenneſs take's away the heart. Hoſ. 4.11. beſot's and infatuate's; rob's a man of himſelf, and laie's a beaſt in his room.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And that yee may teach] The Prieſt's lips ſhould both preſerv knowledg and preſent it to the people; even all the counſel of God. Mal. 2.7. Acts 20.27. To give the knowledg of ſalvation by the remiſſion of ſins. Luke 1.77.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Take the Meat-offering] q. d. Think not that God hath caſhiered you, becauſ hee hath corrected you; neither refuſe your meat out of a ſullen ſowrneſs; but fall to your Meat-offering, and take better heed another time. Onely, eat before the Lord. Deut. 12.18.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And behold it was burnt] Paſſion for their dead friends had ſo tranſported the Prieſts, that they knew not well what they did. Wee uſe to ſaie, Res eſt ingenioſa dolor; but then it muſt not bee exceſſive as here, and as 2 Sam. 18.33.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: To bear the iniquitie] This the ſinner doth ſubjectively, the Prieſt typically, the Lord Chriſt really.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Should it have been accepted] God love's a cheerfull ſerver. Deut. 12.7. and 26.14. Mourners bread is polluted bread. Hoſ. 9.4. And Mal. 2.13. thoſe unkinde husbands are blamed for cauſſing their wives, when they ſhould have been chearfull in God's ſervice, to cover the Lords altar with tears, with weeping and with crying out, ſo that hee regarded not the offering anie more. This Aaron knew, and allegeth for himſelf.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: MAgiſtrate and Miniſter muſt jointly ſee that God's laws bee duly executed. Queen Eliſabeth once in her progreſs viſiting the Countie of Suffolk, all the Juſtices of Peace in that Countie met her Majeſtie; having everie one his Miniſter next to his bodie; which the Queen took ſpecial notice of, and thereupon uttered this ſpeech, that ſhee had often demanded of her Privie Councel, why her Countie of Suffolk was better governed then anie other Countie? and could never underſtand the reaſon thereof; but now ſhee her ſelf perceived the reaſon. It muſt needs be ſo, ſaid ſhee, where Moſes and Aaron, the Word and the Sword go together.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Theſe are the beaſts which yee ſhall eat] Theſe, and theſe onely; 1. That yee may bee at mine appointment for your verie meat, as who am chief Lord of all. 2. That there may bee a difference betwlxt you and all other people. 3. That yee may bee taught to ſtudie puritie, and know that the verie creatures are defiled by man's ſin: 4. That yee may have theſe things as a ſhadow of things to com. Col. 2.16, 17.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Whatſoever parteth the hoof, and cheweth the cud] To teach them to think upon God's commandments to do them. Pſal. 103.18. cleanſing themſelvs from all filthineſs of fleſh and ſpirit. 2 Cor. 7.1.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The camel] The fooliſh Jews when they ſaw Mahomet ariſing in ſuch power, (D. Hall's Peace-maker.) were ſtraight readie to crie him up for their Meſſiah. But when they ſaw him eat of a Camel (ſaith mine Autor) they were as blank as when they ſaw the hoped iſſue of their late Jewiſh Virgin, turn'd to a daughter.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the conie] Which hath his name in Hebrew from hiding himſelf in holes. A weak, but a wiſe creature. Pro. 30.26. And wiſdom is better then ſtrength. Eccleſ. 9.15. The Hare that truſt's to the ſwiftneſs of her legs, is at length taken and torn in pieces. When the Conie that fleets to the rocks doth eaſily avoid the dogs that purſue her. See Iſa. 40.30, 31.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Becauſ hee cheweth the cud, but divideth not] Meditation muſt end in practice: as leſſons of muſick muſt bee practiſed, and a copie not read onely, but written after.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the Swine] Anima ſui data pro ſale, nè carnes putreſcant, ſaid Cleanthes. The Swine hath his ſoul for ſalt onely, ſo hath the drunkard.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Of their fleſh, yee ſhall not eat] Not above the quantitie of an Olive, ſaie the Jew-Doctors, who will need's bee mending magnificat, adding to the Law.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Whatſoever hath fins and ſcales] The fins of the fiſh are for ſteering of their motion, the ſcales for ſmoothneſs of paſſage, (Serm. 1. in die 8. And.) for ſafegard, for ornament. Thoſe onely are clean in the ſight of God, Qui ſquamas & loricam habent patientiae, & pinnulas hilaritatis, ſaith Bernard.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Of all that move in the waters] And yet ſwim alſo in the aër. Like to theſe is the temporarie believer: for that ſeeming to mount up in ſpiritual joies, yet hee withall ſwimmeth, yea batheth himſelf in the waters of ſenſual delights.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: They ſhall bee even an abomination] To teach us, that nothing is lawfull, no not for our common uſe, unleſs it bee ſanctified by the word of God and praier. 1 Tim. 4.5. Acts 10.35.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Eagle] Which yet is counted and called the king of birds, and delight's in high flying. That which is highly eſteemed amongſt men is abomination before God. Lu. 16.15.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the vulture and the kite] That feed upon carrion and dead carcaſſes, and are emblems of greedie gripers and oppreſſors.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Everie raven] Unnatural to his young, whom God himſelf heareth and feedeth. Pſal. 147.9. though they crie with a harſh note, and crie to God by implication; and though the raven bee an inauſpicate bird, and a ſign both of man's puniſhment and God's curſ. Iſa. 34.11.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the owl, and the night-raven] Night-birds that hate the light, or flie againſt it, as bats do, are an abomination. Deeds of darkneſs are out of date, now in the daies of the Goſpel eſpecially. Rom. 13.12, 13.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the cormorant] An unſatisfiable bird, that fitly reſembleth the divel, who daily devour's ſouls, and yet enlargeth his deſires as hell.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the Swan] Whoſe white fethers, but black skin under them, might ſerv to ſet forth the hatefulneſs of hypocriſie.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
And the Stork] Which build's high. Pſal. 104.17. but feed's low on fiſhes, frogs and ſnakes; and ſo might bee the rather rejected, as unfit for food.

And the lapwing] Which is worthily made an hieroglyphick of infelicitie; becauſ it hath as a coronet upon the head, and yet feed's upon the worſt of excrements. It is pittie that the Saints that are brought up in ſcarlet ſhould embrace the dunghill. Lam. 4.5. that anie one that is waſh't in Chriſt's blood, ſhould bedabble his robe in the ſtinking puddle of the world.

And the Bat] Caſt awaie either thy wings or thy teeth (ſaith one to a neuter) and loathing this Bat-like nature, (D. Hall epiſt. to W. L.) bee what thou art, either a bird or a beaſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: All fowls that creep] So all mongrels in religion, that (like the planet Mercurie) can bee good in conjunction with good, and bad with bad; that have religionem Ephemeram, (Hilar.) fidem menſtruam.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Locuſt, &c.] All creeping fowls that go upon all four might not bee eaten, except Arbe, Soleam, Chargol and Chargab, names to us unknown.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Whoſoever toucheth the carcaſs] This and the like ſignified, that all, even the leaſt ſins are to bee purged through Chriſt, and carefully caſt away.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:28
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall waſh his clothes] As having committed a greater ſin, then hee that to ucheth a carcaſs onely. All ſin defileth not alike.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the Tortoiſ] Which hath it's name in Hebrew of a Coach or Wagon: The thick ſhell wherewith it is covered, is ſaid to bee ſo hard, that a loaden Waggon may go over it, and not break it. And ſuch is a hard heart, that cannot repent, or relent never ſo little.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Chamaeleon] A verie fearfull creature, and therefore eaſily turning himſelf into ſundrie colours. Carnal fear put's men upon unwarrancable ſhifts. See Zeph. 3.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:31
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Touch them when they bee dead] There is no kinde of living creature that is defiled whiles it is alive, or that defileth whiles it is alive, ſave man onely, ſaith Maimonie.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:36
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Nevertheleſs a fountain] Becauſ it would cleanſ it ſelf, and work out the uncleanneſs. So will Faith.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:37
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It ſhall bee clean] Becauſ of neceſſitie.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:39
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Of which yee may] Confer Pſalm 49.12. pecoribus morticinis. Tremel.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:40
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall waſh his clothes] To teach them to hate, even the garment ſpotted by the fleſh. Jude 23. all provocations and inſtruments of ſin.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:44
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Yee ſhall bee holie, for I am holie] Great men look to bee ſerved like themſelvs: ſo the great God.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:45
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That bringeth you up] This is often inculcated. God's bleſſings are binders; and everie new deliverance cal's for new obedience.

entries.title: Leviticus 11:47
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: To make a difference] Miniſters alſo in their diſcourſes ſhould put a difference, and take out the pretious from the vile. Jer. 15.19. as did Zuinglius; who when hee inveighed moſt vehemently againſt ſin, would uſually com in with this clauſ, Probe vir, haec nihil ad te. This is not intended to thee, thou godlie man.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
OR yielded ſeed, (Amam. Antibarbar. 575.) as Gen. 1.11. Ʋrgendum hoc adversùs Anabaptiſtas; qui, ut ſuos de humanae Chriſti naturae origine errores ſtabiliunt, foeminas ſemen habere praefractè negant.

Then ſhee ſhall bee unclean] This ſignified that corruption of man's nature, wherein hee is conceived. (Auguſtin.) Pſal. 51.5. (being condemned aſſoon as conceived, Damnatus antequam natus) and the remedie wee have in Chriſt.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And in the eighth daie] See the Note on Gen. 17.13, 14.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shee ſhall touch no hallowed thing] Preparation muſt go before participation of holie ordinances. Hag. 2.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But if ſhee bear a maid-childe] To intimate, it may bee, the womans beeing firſt in the tranſgreſſion. 1 Tim. 2.14.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And when the daies of her purifying] The Virgin Marie alſo obſerved this Law. Luke 2.21. not in conſcience of anie particular ſin, which in the conception of our Saviour, ſhee was free from; nor in ſhew, to ſatisfie the law; much leſs upon hypocriſie; but in conſcience of her natural corruption; which by this oblation, according to the Law, ſhee did confeſs holily and religiouſly before God and his Congregation, as one well obſerveth.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And make an attonement] Whereby her faith was confirmed, that by Chriſt her ſin was remitted, and the curſ removed. 1 Tim. 2.15.

entries.title: Leviticus 12:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And if ſhee bee not able] As the bleſſed Virgin was not. Luke 2.22, 24. who now can deſpiſe anie one for want, when the mother of our Lord was not rich enough to bring a Lamb for her purification? Wee may bee as happie in ruſſet, as in tiſſue.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: SEE the Note on Levit. 7.22.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Like the plague of leproſie] Leproſie is both an effect and type of ſin; which is ſuch a ſickneſs of the ſoul, as thoſe are of the bodie, which Phyſicians ſaie are Corruptio totius ſubſtantia, univerſal diſeaſes, tending to the iſſues of death. It drie's up and draw's out the verie vital blood and life of the ſoul.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
The plague in the skin of the fleſh] That is, the white, bright ſpot, verſ 2. Confer Exod. 4.6. Numb. 12.10.

Is turned white] This might note ſuch as have continued long, and are aged in anie wickedneſs.

Bee deeper then the skin of his fleſh] Compare Numb. 12.12. 2 Kings 5.14. Such are they, whoſe wickedneſs is not onely acted by their hands, but ſeated in their hearts, and ſunk into their ſpirits: like the ſpots of the leopard, which no art can cure, no water waſh off, becauſ they are not in the skin, but in the fleſh and bones, in the ſinews and moſt inner parts. Ingrained diſeaſes are not eaſily ſtirred, much leſs deſtroied.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shall ſhut him up] For further trial of truth, that daughter of time. Wee may not precipitate a cenſure, but bee ſlow to ſpeak, ſlow to wrath. The leper muſt bee ſhut up from week to week, till the thing were certain: So till mens perverſneſs bee made manifeſt. 2 Tim. 3.9. wee muſt ſuſpend our cenſures. Manie are like candles whoſe tallow is mixt with brine; no ſooner lighted, but they ſpit up and down the room.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Spred not in the skin] So if men mend by admonition, and take up in time; if they refuſe not to bee reformed, hate not to bee healed, as Babylon. Jer. 51.9. as Ephraïm. Hoſ. 7.1. When I would have healed Ephraïm, then the iniquitie of Ephraïm was diſcovered, or brake out as a leproſie in his fore-head. See Ezekiel 24.13.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
It is but a ſcab] Such as may bee the ſpot of God's children. Deut. 32.5. Sin make's wicked men the object of Gods hatred, the Saints of his pitie; as wee hate poiſon in a toad, but wee pitie it in a man.

And hee ſhall waſh his clothes] The beſt cannot waſh in innocencie, hee muſt therefore waſh in tears. Iſa. 1.16. God alſo will ſet in and waſh ſuch with the blood of his ſon.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But if the ſcab ſpread] So if ſin bee gaining and growing ſtill upon the ſinner, even after admonition; or is ſcattered and ſpread to the infecting of others, it is a verie ill ſign.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall bee brought unto the Prieſt] Who was to diſcern it by the law of leproſie: (Rom. 3.20. & 7.7.) ſo muſt wee finde out our ſins by the moral law. Rom. 3. The works of the fleſh are manifeſt. Gal. 5. Neither need wee half ſo much caution or curioſitie to bee perſuaded of our ſpiritual leproſie, which is too too apparent: onely thoſe manie cerimonies (as one well noteth) may put us in minde how much more exquiſite our diligence ought to bee in finding and ferreting out our ſpecial ſins.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And there bee quick raw fleſh] It is one of the moſt remarkable things in all this law (ſaith a learned Divine) that quick or ſound fleſh in the ſore ſhould bee judged leproſie, and the man unclean: whereas if the leproſie covered all his fleſh, hee was pronounced clean, verſ 13. Hereby, 1. May bee meant ſuch as juſtifie themſelvs and their wickedneſs, as Jonas did his anger; whereas hee was judged himſelf, is like him who had the leproſie all over, and might bee declared clean. Or, 2. Such who ſin againſt the light of knowledg, and the quickning, yea rawneſs of a galled conſcience.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And if a leproſie] So called, becauſ ſo counted at firſt: but it prove's no more then a kinde of ſcurf or ſcab.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall pronounce him clean] i. e. not infectiouſly or incurably unclean.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But when raw fleſh] Becauſ it ſhew'd that there were ſtill corrupt and poiſoned humors in the bodie, not eaſie to bee expelled till death.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It is a leproſie] Properly ſo called, a fretting ſoreneſs or ſcabbedneſs. The Greeks call it Elephas or Elephantiaſis, when the skin grow's hard as the Elephant's skin. This the Iſraëlites brought (likely) out of Aegypt; for it was bred onely about Nilus, and is therefore called the botch of Aegypt. Deut. 28.27.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Turn again] Viz. to bee white like the reſt of the bodie: ſo if a ſinner ſtop or ſtep back, &c.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Was a bile and is healed] Seemed to bee healed, as apoſtates to have eſcaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledg of Chriſt. 2 Pet. 2.20. and to have known the waie of righteouſneſs, verſ 21. and yet the later end is worſ with them then the begining. They becom altogether filthie. Pſalm 53.3. Forſakers of the Covenant, yea, wicked doers againſt the Covenant. Dan. 11.30, 32. Theſe ſin not common ſins, as Core and his companie died not common deaths.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And if it ſpread much abroad] So, if ſin reign there is no pardon: rebel it may, reign it muſt not.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But if the bright ſpot ſtaie] Sin, if it reign not is not imputed; for wee are not under the law, but under grace. Rom. 6.12, 14.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A leproſie broken out of the burning] Seldom do paſſions burn, but there is a leproſie breaking out of that burning; ſuch as cauſſeth the climate where ſuch lepers live to be like the torrid Zone, too hot for anie to live neer them.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A yellow thin hair] Which is a true ſign of a skall.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:34
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall waſh his clothes] See the Note on ver. 6.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:35
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: After his cleanſing] See the Note on ver. 18.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:37
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Black hair] A ſign of ſoundneſs. Quod ſanitas in corpore, id ſanctitas in corde, ſaith Bernard.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:39
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A freckled ſpot] Or white-morphew. This made not a man unclean: no more do meer infirmities make God abhor us.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:44
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: His plague is in his head] Such a leper is everie ignorant man; how much more the man that is an heretick? whom therefore after the firſt and ſecond admonition wee muſt reject. Titus 3.10. yea from ſuch ſtand off. 1 Tim. 6.5. Keep aloof as from lepers, (Purchas Pilgr.) their verie breath is infectious; and like the dogs of Congo, they bite, though they bark not.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:45
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
His clothes ſhall bee rent] To ſhew his ſorrow for ſin, the cauſ of his calamitie.

And his head bare] That men might not miſtake him; and further to ſhew his humilitie, whereof this alſo was a cerimonie.

A covering upon his upper lip] His Moucbaches, that by his breath hee might not inſect others: and to ſhew that God will not hear a good motion from an ill mouth.

Ʋnclean, unclean] Saie wee the ſame in our humbleſt acknowledgments; but withall add that of the leper in the Goſpel, Yet Lord, if thou wilt, thou canſt make mee clean.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:46
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Without the Camp] And that utterly, if incurable, as Ʋzzias. A livelie type of Excommunication, which the Apoſtle deſcribeth. 2 Cor. 5.11, 12. and our Saviour. Mat. 18.17.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:47
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The garment alſo] A plague not anie where elſ read or heard of: beeing nothing like clothes now-adaies infected with the plague, but far more ſtrange and dangerous, whether it did ſpread or fret inward, the garment was to bee burnt with fire. This ſignified that all inſtruments of idolatrie, or of anie other ſin are to bee deſtroied, and made awaie. As the Law commandeth, The graven images of their gods ſhall yee burn with fire. Deut. 7.25, 26. And Jude alludeth to it, when hee biddeth us ſave ſom with fear, pulling them out of the fire, bating even the garment ſpotted by the fleſh. Jude 23. See Iſa. 30.22. Acts 19.19. Juſticiaries alſo ſhall one daie finde, that though to the worldward they waſh themſelvs with ſnow-water, and make their hands never ſo clean, yet God will plunge them in the ditch, and their own clothes ſhall make them to bee abhorred. Job 9.30, 31.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: ANd to Aaron alſo though not here mentioned, as hee is, verſ 33.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall bee brought unto the Prieſt] To teach us to go to Jeſus Chriſt the high-Prieſt of our profeſſion, who healeth all our diſeaſes. Pſalm 103.3. He cured the leproſie (to others altogether incurable) by a touch of his hand onely. Mark 1.41. Yea hee ſent his word and healed them. Pſalm 107.20. and ſo hee doth the ſouls of ſinners that com unto him.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: If the plague of leproſie bee healed] As it was in Simon the leper that entertained Chriſt. Jealouſie, Phrenſie and Hereſie are counted incurable diſeaſes: not ſo leproſie; though the moſt carried it to their death, as Gehazi, Azariah, &c.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Command to take] That the leper might ſhew his thankfulneſs to Jehovah his Phyſician, as hee is called. Exod. 15.26. See Mat. 8.4. Men praie and paie Phyſicians of their bodies, who yet do but officiosè occidere manie times. And ſhall God have nothing? Muſt hee ask as once, Where are the other nine? Shall wee not turn again with Naaman now cleanſed, and offer our ſervice, renounce our idols, dedicate all wee are and have to the God of Iſraël?

Two birds] Or ſparrows, whereof two were ſold for a farthing: to ſhew how lightly ſet by Chriſt is in the world, whoſe blood nevertheleſs is more worth then a thouſand worlds.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Over running water] Heb. Living water. Life conſiſt's in motion, in action: hence waters that ſpring and run are, for their continual motion, called living waters. O Lord, ſaith Hezekiah, By theſe things men live, and in all theſe things is the life of my ſpirit. Iſa. 38.16.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That was killed over the running water] Pointing at Chriſt, who came not by water onely, but by water and blood. 1 John 5.6. See the Note there, and on 1 Cor. 6.11.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
And hee ſhall ſprinkle] This led them to that blood of ſprinkling. Heb. 12.23. applied unto them by that hyſopbunch of faith, whereby the heart is purified.

And ſhall let the living bird looſ] This figured (ſale ſom) that neither Chriſt's deïtie without the ſhedding of his blood, nor Chriſt's blood (but for the quickning life of the God-head, perſonally dwelling in him) could have been available for the purging of ſin. Both which himſelf declareth. John 6.53, with 63. And hither belongeth 2 Cor. 5.19. Acts 20.28. Moreover it figured, that Chriſt by his death conquered him that had the power of death. Heb. 2.15. whileſt hee fled as a bird to the everlaſting mountains, from the jaws of death to the joies of heaven. Heb. 7.26.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Shall waſh his clothes and ſhave] This the leper was to do the firſt daie of his cleanſing; (1 Tim. 6.18.) to teach men to bee thorough in the practice of mortification, at the firſt converſion: laying a good foundation for the time to com, that they may laie hold on eternal life.

And ſhall tarrie abroad] Men muſt not bee too haſtie at firſt to catch at comfort; but let humiliation have her perfect work, and our ſorrows bee ſutable to our ſins.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: (Ezra 10.13.) Even all his hair hee ſhall ſhave off] To ſhew that repentance and mortification is not the work of a daie (as hee ſaid in another caſe) but of a man's whole life. There muſt bee a dailie ſhaving and paring of luſts and ſuperfluities; which are to the ſoul as excrements are to the bodie. Yea, the more a ſinner is exerciſed in mortification, the more hee ſearcheth out his corruptions. Now hee ſhaveth off the hair not of his head onely, but of his beard and eie-brows.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee ſhall take two hee-lambs] That by theſe ſacrifices hee might bee taught to ſeek for the cleanſing of his ſoul, together with the healing of his bodie; that there might bee mens ſana in corpore ſano, a cure don on both inſide and outſide too.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: At the door of the tabernacle] There God is to bee found, viz. in the publick aſſemblies, and that wee are indeed (ſaith one) when wee are at the door of the Tabernacle.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And wave them] This may note, 1. Chriſt's extreme ſufferings. 2. The waving of Chriſt in the preaching of the Goſpel. 3. The motion of the ſinner's lips in confeſſion and ſupplication.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It is moſt holie] The waie of holineſs, in and by Chriſt is an abſolute waie, as ever was deviſed.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the tip of the right ear] To ſignifie that all Chriſt's ſanctified ones have a hearing ear, an active hand, a nimble foot, to walk in the waie that is called holie.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Som of the log] Chriſt's comforts muſt bee warily propounded to men, and with good diſcretion.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Seven times] This might note the perfection of the joies God hath for his, and our imperfection in believing it, in that it was ſo manie times ſprinkled.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the tip of the right ear] To aſſure him of comfort, in hearing, doing, perſevering.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Ʋpon the head] Everlaſting joie ſhall bee upon the heads of Chriſt's ranſomed ones. Iſa. 35. ult.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And afterwards the burnt-offering] Wee muſt bee reconciled by Chriſt (our ſin-offering) before the ſacrificing of our ſelvs (which is our reaſonable ſervice) can bee accepted.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And the meat-offering] The meat-offering annexed to the burnt-offering ſhew's (ſaith one) either that Chriſtians grow marvellouſly in this life, (Bifield on 1 Pet. 1.22.) after they have full aſſurance of pardon of ſin: or elſ that Chriſt will bee their eternal food in heaven.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And if hee bee poor] Here's a proviſo for poor people: God make's no difference, but accept's of a little where much is not to bee had.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:32
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Whoſe hand is not able to get] This is often urged, to ſhew, that the beſt can bee got muſt not bee thought too good for God: and that if through careleſneſs or niggardice men do not their utmoſt, that's a juſt exception.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:34
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Plague of leproſie in a houſ] Such is the contagion of ſin, that it will infect the verie houſ wee dwell in, the garments wee wear, even all the creatures wee uſe, ſo as all things are to us impure. Titus 1.13. even the houſ of God alſo. Levit. 16.16. and his holie ordinances. The Canaanites had defiled the land from one end to another with their uncleanneſſes. Ezra 9.11. and ſo infected the air. This Law taught men; 1. Upon all occaſions to ſhew their utter deteſtation of ſin, but eſpecially of idolatrie. 2. To take heed of deſpiſing admonition, leſt they bee utterly ruined, and that without remedie. Prov. 29.1.

entries.title: Leviticus 15:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: AN involuntarie flux of ſeed, ſuch as David imprecateth upon Joab, 2 Sam. 3.29.

entries.title: Leviticus 15:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It is his uncleanneſs] Hereby they were taught the turpitude of ſin, of original ſin eſpecially, that peccatum peccans, as the Scholes call it; that ſinfull ſin, as S. Paul. Rom. 7.13. for ſo filthie it is, that hee can call it no worſ then by it's own name, as wanting a fitter Epithite.

entries.title: Leviticus 15:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Everie bed] Sin is more catching then anie plague, and more defiling then anie jakes. Mark 7.23. Paul found it as noiſom to his ſoul, as a dead bodie to his ſenſ. Rom. 7.24. or as the ſanies of a plague-ſore to a rich robe. Job abhor's himſelf for it in duſt and aſhes. Chap. 40.4. And Iſaiah look's upon himſelf as an undon man, by reaſon of it, Chap. 6.5.

entries.title: Leviticus 15:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Spit upon him] Noting the pollution that com's to men's ſouls by thoſe that ſpit hereſies, and belch out blaſphemies.

entries.title: Leviticus 15:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
